This compares with net earnings of $80 million, or 11 cents per diluted share, on net sales of $1.7 billion for the same period last year and net earnings of $162 million for second quarter 2026. There were no special items in third quarter 2026. Net earnings before special items was $40 million for the same period last year and $91 million for second quarter 2026. Adjusted EBITDA for third quarter 2026 was $248 million, compared with $217 million for the same period last year and $310 million for second quarter 2026. In October, Weyerhaeuser entered into an agreement to divest approximately 81,000 acres of non-core timberlands in Arkansas for $146 million. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter and is subject to customary closing conditions. Consistent with the company’s long-standing approach to active portfolio management, Weyerhaeuser will continue to evaluate opportunities to optimize the return profile of its timberlands portfolio, while also creating additional flexibility for broader capital allocation and growth priorities as market conditions and opportunities evolve. “Our teams delivered solid operating performance in the third quarter against an increasingly challenging macroeconomic backdrop,” said Devin W. Stockfish, president and chief executive officer. “In addition, we continued to enhance the value of our timberlands portfolio and made meaningful progress advancing several strategic growth initiatives. Looking ahead, we remain confident in the longer-term demand fundamentals that support growth for our businesses and are well positioned to navigate the current environment given the strength of our portfolio, balance sheet and flexible capital allocation framework. We remain intently focused on driving operational excellence, serving our customers and executing our strategy to create superior long-term value for our shareholders.” WEYERHAEUSER FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS 2026 2026 2025 (millions, except per share data) Q2 Q3 Q3 Net sales $ 1,867 $ 1,862 $ 1,717 Net earnings $ 162 $ 61 $ 80 Net earnings per diluted share $ 0.23 $ 0.08 $ 0.11 Weighted average shares outstanding, diluted 722 721 722 Net earnings before special items (1)(2) $ 91 $ 61 $ 40 Net earnings per diluted share before special items (1) $ 0.13 $ 0.08 $ 0.06 Adjusted EBITDA (1) $ 310 $ 248 $ 217 Net cash from operations $ 399 $ 193 $ 210 Adjusted FAD (3) $ 323 $ 110 $ 117 1 (1) Net earnings before special items is a non-GAAP measure that management believes provides helpful context in understanding the company’s earnings performance. Additionally, Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure that management uses to evaluate the performance of the company. Adjusted EBITDA, as we define it, is operating income adjusted for depreciation, depletion, amortization, basis of Strategic Land Solutions acres sold and special items. Net earnings before special items and Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered in isolation from, and are not intended to represent an alternative to, our GAAP results. Reconciliations of net earnings before special items and Adjusted EBITDA to GAAP earnings are included within this release. (2) Special items for prior periods presented are included in the reconciliation tables within this release. (3) Adjusted Funds Available for Distribution (Adjusted FAD) is a non-GAAP measure that management uses to evaluate the company’s liquidity. Adjusted FAD, as we define it, is net cash from operations adjusted for capital expenditures and significant non-recurring items. Adjusted FAD measures cash generated during the period (net of capital expenditures and significant non-recurring items) that is available for dividends, repurchases of common shares, debt reduction, acquisitions and other discretionary and nondiscretionary capital allocation activities. Adjusted FAD should not be considered in isolation from, and is not intended to represent an alternative to, our GAAP results. A reconciliation of Adjusted FAD to net cash from operations is included within this release. TIMBERLANDS FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS 2026 2026 (millions) Q2 Q3 Change Net sales $ 518 $ 531 $ 13 Net contribution to pretax earnings $ 130 $ 67 $ (63 ) Pretax benefit for special items $ (71 ) $ — $ 71 Net contribution to pretax earnings before special items $ 59 $ 67 $ 8 Adjusted EBITDA $ 123 $ 133 $ 10 Q3 2026 Performance – In the West, fee harvest volumes and forestry and road costs were comparable to the second quarter. Sales volumes were lower primarily due to fiber logs and the timing of export vessels, and per unit log and haul costs were also lower due to fewer export shipments. Sales realizations were slightly higher. In the South, fee harvest volumes were significantly higher than the second quarter due to more favorable weather conditions. Sales realizations were slightly lower due to mix. Per unit log and haul costs were also slightly lower, and forestry and road costs were seasonally higher. Q4 2026 Outlook – Weyerhaeuser anticipates fourth quarter earnings before special items and Adjusted EBITDA will be comparable to the third quarter. In the West, the company expects slightly lower fee harvest volumes and slightly higher sales volumes, primarily for export. Sales realizations are expected to be slightly lower. Per unit log and haul costs are expected to be comparable, with seasonally lower forestry and road costs. In the South, the company expects moderately lower fee harvest volumes, slightly higher sales realizations and per unit log and haul costs, and comparable forestry and road costs. STRATEGIC LAND SOLUTIONS FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS 2026 2026 (millions) Q2 Q3 Change Net sales $ 140 $ 99 $ (41 ) Net contribution to pretax earnings $ 94 $ 67 $ (27 ) Adjusted EBITDA $ 129 $ 86 $ (43 ) Q3 2026 Performance – Earnings and Adjusted EBITDA decreased from the second quarter due to the timing and mix of Real Estate sales. The number of acres sold decreased significantly, and the average price per acre was moderately lower. The company’s Real Estate results are typically more heavily weighted toward the first half of the year. Q4 2026 Outlook – Weyerhaeuser anticipates fourth quarter earnings before special items will be approximately $35 million lower than the third quarter and Adjusted EBITDA will be approximately $45 million lower than the third quarter due to the timing and mix of Real Estate sales. The company continues to expect full year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to be approximately $450 million, a $25 million increase from the initial outlook, and basis as a percentage of Strategic Land Solutions sales to be 15 to 20 percent for the full year. 2 WOOD PRODUCTS FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS 2026 2026 (millions) Q2 Q3 Change Net sales $ 1,360 $ 1,385 $ 25 Net contribution to pretax earnings $ 71 $ 32 $ (39 ) Adjusted EBITDA $ 129 $ 91 $ (38 ) Q3 2026 Performance – For lumber, delivered sales realizations were slightly higher compared with the second quarter average. Sales volumes were moderately higher and log and unit manufacturing costs were slightly higher. For oriented strand board, sales realizations were 2 percent lower compared with the second quarter average. Sales volumes were slightly lower, fiber costs were comparable, and unit manufacturing costs were moderately higher due to more extensive planned annual maintenance and elevated resin costs. For engineered wood products, sales volumes were slightly higher for most products compared to the second quarter. Raw material and unit manufacturing costs were also slightly higher. Sales realizations were lower overall, partially driven by a mix shift within solid section products, but were higher for plywood. For distribution, results were lower than the second quarter, primarily due to decreased sales volumes and margins on specialty products. Q4 2026 Outlook – Weyerhaeuser anticipates fourth quarter earnings before special items and Adjusted EBITDA will be moderately lower than the third quarter, excluding the effect of changes in average sales realizations for lumber and oriented strand board. For lumber, the company expects slightly lower sales volumes and slightly higher log and unit manufacturing costs. For oriented strand board, the company anticipates slightly higher sales volumes and fiber costs and slightly lower unit manufacturing costs. For engineered wood products, the company expects slightly higher sales realizations, slightly lower sales volumes for most products and moderately higher raw material costs. For distribution, the company anticipates slightly lower results compared to the third quarter. ABOUT WEYERHAEUSER Weyerhaeuser Company, one of the world's largest private owners of timberlands, began operations in 1900 and today owns or controls more than 10 million acres of timberlands in the U.S., as well as additional public timberlands managed under long-term licenses in Canada. Weyerhaeuser has been a global leader in sustainability for more than a century and manages 100 percent of its timberlands on a fully sustainable basis in compliance with internationally recognized sustainable forestry standards. Weyerhaeuser is also one of the largest manufacturers of wood products in North America and operates additional business lines around product distribution, climate solutions, real estate, and energy and natural resources, among others. In 2025, the company generated $6.9 billion in net sales and employed approximately 9,500 people who serve customers worldwide. Operated as a real estate investment trust, Weyerhaeuser’s common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol WY. Learn more at www.weyerhaeuser.com.
